timeline.title: CMS-4201-F applies
timeline.body: The final rule (88 FR 22120) applies to coverage beginning January 1, 2024. MA plans must follow traditional Medicare coverage criteria. These include the inpatient admission payment criteria at 42 CFR 412.3 and the coverage criteria for skilled nursing, home health and inpatient rehabilitation.

timeline.title: Senate subcommittee majority staff report
timeline.body: The majority staff of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations reported that UnitedHealthcare, Humana and CVS denied post-acute care prior authorization requests at higher rates than other care in 2022. UnitedHealthcare's initial denial rate for skilled nursing facility requests rose from 1.4 percent in 2019 to 12.6 percent in 2022.

timeline.title: Insurer prior authorization pledge
timeline.body: Health plans, through AHIP, committed to six actions on prior authorization, covering commercial, Medicare Advantage and Medicaid managed care coverage. The commitments are voluntary. CMS and HHS announced the pledge the same day.

timeline.title: CMS-0057-F shorter standard deadline begins
timeline.body: For items and services subject to prior authorization, impacted payers, including MA plans, must now send standard decisions within seven calendar days instead of 14. The 72-hour deadline for expedited requests already applied. MA plans may extend a standard decision by up to 14 calendar days in some cases, such as when the enrollee asks for it.

timeline.body: MedPAC reported that MA stays averaged about 5.7 days against 5.2 for traditional Medicare in FY2024. After adjustment, the gap was 11.2 percent overall and 32.3 percent for stays ending in an inpatient rehabilitation facility.

plans.text: Using 2018 claims, a 2023 study found MA enrollees were 6 percent less likely than traditional Medicare patients to be hospitalized for conditions that good outpatient care can often prevent (relative risk 0.94). Plans argue that if fewer of their healthier members are admitted, the MA patients who are admitted may be sicker, and stay longer for reasons other than delay.

assumptions.label: Variable cost of one extra day
assumptions.why: About a quarter of KFF's $3,297 expense per adjusted inpatient day (2024, from the AHA Annual Survey), on the reasoning that most staffing, overhead and capital costs do not change with one more low-acuity day. One academic center study found the last full day of a stay cost $420 in 1990s dollars, or 2.4 percent of total stay cost. MedPAC says some hospital costs are fixed and do not rise with a longer stay.

assumptions.label: Share of freed bed-days refilled
assumptions.why: An assumption: the share rises from 0% at 70% occupancy to 100% at 90%. National staffed-bed occupancy was 75.3% in the year after the public health emergency, and 85% is a shortage threshold in the Leuchter model. In a hospital benchmarking study, boarding exceeded 4 hours in 88.9% of hospital-months when occupancy passed 85%. Median occupancy in the FY2024 cost reports is 58.3%, which suggests available beds exceed staffed beds. Override this if your hospital routinely turns patients away.

assumptions.label: Where MA patients go after discharge
assumptions.value: Home 65%, home health 17%, skilled nursing 15%, inpatient rehabilitation 3%
assumptions.why: From MedPAC's 2023 data: 65, 17 and 15 percent for home, home health and skilled nursing, and 3 percent for inpatient rehabilitation (5 percent in traditional Medicare). MedPAC shows long-term care hospitals separately, at under 1 percent of MA discharges, and the model leaves them out.

assumptions.label: Which gap counts as extra days
assumptions.why: Unadjusted and adjusted gaps by discharge destination come from MedPAC Table 4-1. The placement lens is the adjusted gap minus the adjusted gap for patients discharged home, so it shows the extra stay length associated with post-acute placement. MedPAC describes these gaps as associations and says they suggest that plans could slow discharges through activities such as prior authorization.
